samples.summary: No test joins the new service-token signer to the verifier that must accept it
samples.evidence: `auth.service.ts` was changed so `verifyYorkieToken` accepts `typ === YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE`, and `yorkie-service-token.ts` mints that token with its own DI-free `JwtService`. The `describe('Yorkie tokens')` block in auth.service.spec.ts (lines 59–105) round-trips only `issueYorkieUserToken` and `issueYorkieShareToken`; there is no case feeding `signYorkieServiceToken(secret, ...)` into `service.verifyYorkieToken(...)`. The only place a service token is verified in tests is yorkie.service.spec.ts:189, which uses a bare `new JwtService().verify(...)` rather than `AuthService`, so the two ends are never connected. The controller spec that exercises the new allow-branch (yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts:123) stubs `verifyYorkieToken` out entirely. If the signing and verifying halves ever disagree (secret source, claim shape, expiry option, an added issuer/audience check), every server-side attach — v1 content endpoints, DocumentCopyService, template publish/seed — 401s on any deployment that registered the webhook methods, and nothing in the suite would notice.
searchedFor: glob packages/backend/src/yorkie/*.ts for a yorkie-service-token spec

samples.summary: 'still refuses a service token that does not verify' exercises nothing service-specific — it duplicates the existing invalid-token test
samples.evidence: The test builds `makeController({ identity: 'throw' })`, i.e. the stubbed `verifyYorkieToken` throws for any input; the token string 'forged' is never parsed. It is mechanically identical to the pre-existing '401s on an invalid/expired token for a doc method' (line 99), differing only in the token literal and verb. The real property it claims to pin — that an unsigned/forged `yorkie-service` payload is rejected — lives in `AuthService.verifyYorkieToken`, which is mocked away here and untested for that type (see the auth.service.spec finding). It reads as coverage of the new service-token branch while covering none of it.

samples.summary: Vacuous assertions for the new `canUndo`/`canRedo` read-only guard
samples.evidence: The new test 'lets no write reach the store on a read-only mount' ends with `expect(api.canUndo()).toBe(false)` and `expect(api.canRedo()).toBe(false)`. The store is a freshly constructed `MemNoteStore('hello')` and every preceding call was blocked, so `store.canUndo()`/`canRedo()` are already `false` (MemNoteStore's undo/redo stacks start empty — memory.ts:189-195). Both assertions therefore hold identically with or without the `!readOnly &&` guard added at editor.ts:674-675, so the new behaviour (a toolbar host being told there is nothing to revert on a viewer mount) is not actually covered. Nothing seeds history on the underlying store before wrapping to make the guard observable.

samples.summary: No spec for yorkie-service-token.ts: the no-secret fallbacks and env-driven expiry are untested
samples.evidence: There is no `yorkie-service-token.spec.ts` (glob over packages/backend/src/yorkie/*.ts). Untested branches: `yorkieServiceTokenInjector(undefined)` returning `undefined`; `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv()` warning and returning `undefined` when `JWT_SECRET` is unset (the path all three ops scripts take); the `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` env cast. The matching branch in YorkieService (yorkie.service.ts, `else { this.logger.warn(...) }`) is also unreachable in tests because `createMockConfigService` in yorkie.service.spec.ts:37 always returns a JWT_SECRET. Failure here is a silently anonymous attach rather than a loud error, which is exactly the case the diff says the webhook will refuse.

samples.summary: The split-divider changes (hit area, touch-action, drag-ratio math) have no test at all
samples.evidence: `grep 'divider|splitRatio|pointerdown'` over packages/notes/src/view/editor.test.ts returns no matches — there are no divider tests before or after this diff. The diff changes user-visible drag behaviour: width 7px→25px with 12px padding, `touchAction = 'none'` (without which a finger drag never resizes at all), and the ratio denominator from `rect.width` to `rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`. A regression in the ratio math (divider trailing the pointer, or panes jumping) or a dropped `touch-action` would ship unnoticed. jsdom makes offsetWidth degenerate, but a pointerdown/pointermove test could still pin the applied flex-basis and the style properties.
searchedFor: read the new tests in editor.test.ts

samples.summary: NotesView's new read-only store wrapping is not covered by any test
samples.evidence: notes-view.tsx now does `const store = readOnly ? readOnlyNoteStore(raw) : raw`. The only new frontend test in this diff (shared-notes-layout.test.tsx) mocks `@/app/notes/notes-view` away entirely (lines 96-118), and grep for `readOnlyNoteStore` finds no frontend test file. So nothing asserts that a viewer mount hands the engine a neutered handle, nor that a non-readOnly mount still hands it the writable one (a wrapping-condition inversion would silently make the workspace note editor read-only). The wrapper itself and `initialize()`'s own wrap are tested in packages/notes, so the blast radius is limited to this call site.
searchedFor: grep 'readOnlyNoteStore|readOnlyDocStore' repo-wide (12 files, no frontend test)

samples.summary: read-only store test calls setLocalSelection and never asserts it was neutered; subscribePresence forwarding untested
samples.evidence: 'neuters every write path' calls `view.setLocalSelection(1, 2)` at line 41 but asserts only `store.getText()` and `store.canUndo()` afterwards — neither observes the selection, so the documented guarantee ('a viewer's caret is not something a read-only mount owes its peers', read-only.ts:~150) is unasserted. MemNoteStore's `currentSelection` is private but is observable indirectly through a subsequent undo unit's restored selection. Separately, `subscribePresence` is in NOTE_STORE_READERS but no test exercises it; if it were mis-classified as a mutator, remote-caret updates would silently stop on every viewer mount (`getPeerSelections` alone would still pass line 18).
searchedFor: read packages/notes/src/store/memory.ts for observable selection state

samples.evidence: The assertion only rules out the literal substring `token=`; a log line that interpolated the bearer value under any other label (or bare) would pass. The test already has the token value ('t') to hand, so asserting the value's absence — or better, a distinctive token literal — would actually pin 'the token must never join the target in a log'. As written it guards a format string rather than the secret.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: repo-wide grep shows `verifyYorkieToken` is called in tests only at auth.service.spec.ts:67,75,87,94,103 (user token, share token, replayed access token, garbage, expired) — never with a token from `signYorkieServiceToken`. The new accept-branch at auth.service.ts:99-105 (`payload.typ !== YORKIE_SERVICE_TOKEN_TYPE`) is therefore uncovered. The only test touching a real service token, yorkie.service.spec.ts:186-191, verifies it with a bare `new JwtService().verify(token, { secret: JWT_SECRET })`, not through AuthService, so it cannot catch a divergence in secret source, claim shape, expiry option, or an added issuer/audience check. yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts stubs AuthService entirely (lines 29, 293, 325) and line 124 injects an already-decoded `{ typ: 'yorkie-service' }` identity. I also searched outside the reviewer's paths: packages/backend/test/** e2e suites; only revision-history.e2e-spec.ts calls the real webhook and it uses issueYorkieUserToken/issueYorkieShareToken (lines 422-423, 430, 499), never a service token. Removing the service-token clause from auth.service.ts:102 would leave the suite green while every server-side attach 401s under an enforcing webhook — a silently weakened/changed guard with no meaningful test, major under this rubric.
